newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus PM resigns, president names successor.
newsitem.headline: Belarus PM resigns, president names successor.

text.p: Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko, locked in a fierce battle for power with parliament, said on Monday he had accepted the resignation of his prime minister, Mikhail Chigir.

Lukashenko, whose critics accuse him of trying to set up a dictatorship in the former Soviet republic, told state television the current deputy prime minister reponsible for economic and finance issues, Sergei Ling, would replace Chigir.
The 42-year-old president, who hopes to boost his powers in a referendum that ends on Sunday, said his labour minister Alexander Sosnov had also resigned from the government.
Earlier Chigir, until now a Lukashenko loyalist, had met parliamentary leaders who quoted him as saying he would resign unless the president cancelled his referendum.

Chigir is a well-respected figure in the republic of 10 million people. Lukashenko appointed him prime minister after winning a landslide election in July 1994 with promises to wipe out corruption and rebuild ties with neighbouring Russia.
His departure could deal a big blow to Lukashenko's campaign to tighten his grip on rival institutions, including parliament and the constitutional court, political analysts said.
